description: Services emit logs and return values but no typed completion/state-change events Environment can subscribe to. Session effects rely on a git-poll adapter and invocation-result envelopes.
desired_contract: Typed, subscribable completion/state events per owning service.
effect: Poll-based sources only; provider push notification is not yet available.
evidence: mncs-environment/mncs_env/sources.py generic Source contract with live store-replay, git-heads, commons-sync, and language-service sources; no provider push bus found
title: No canonical provider event feeds
why_not_local: Event semantics belong to the owning services; an environment-local bus would become a competing standard.
workaround: Background reconciler polls typed sources with durable cursors and Store replay-across-downtime; subscriptions replay from the session log.

description: Nothing in MNCS records which agent owns a worktree or branch. Environment keeps a local advisory lease file enforced only inside its own authority evaluation.
desired_contract: Family lease record (holder, scope, expiry, release) readable without joining Environment.
effect: Cross-harness ownership is voluntary; Environment-side conflicts deny inside its own authority evaluation.
evidence: control/leases.py exists but is service-local; no family lease contract found
title: No canonical workspace lease/ownership mechanism
why_not_local: Cross-agent ownership must be authoritative family-wide; a local file cannot bind other harnesses.
workaround: claims v2 (repository/worktree/path scopes, conflict denial, dirty-adoption, liveness) + Control worktree surface; unknown work is never touched.

description: Session authority is projected from intent constraints and protected scopes. Canonical authorization semantics live in mncs-rights-provenance, which Environment does not yet bind.
desired_contract: Machine-checkable grant query (subject, action, scope).
effect: AuthorityContext is intent-declared; escalation paths are explicit but human-mediated.
evidence: No machine grant-check endpoint was consumable from survey
title: Rights/provenance granularity for session authority
why_not_local: Replacing rights evaluation would be security theater and a competing authorization universe.
workaround: Pure evaluate() with default-deny; every denial/escalation is an event.

description: Intent, authority projection, lifecycle, and checkpoints are JSON contracts over host infrastructure.
desired_contract: Stable file-effect + record-schema story for Environment projection inside MNCS.
effect: Canonical semantics live in Python with JSON contracts; migration path stays open.
evidence: docs/MODEL.md native-MNCS section
title: Environment concepts have no native MNCS representation yet
why_not_local: Forcing immature language features would block useful infrastructure for ideological purity.
workaround: JSON contracts are canonical; host code is transport/discovery only.

description: Real entry discovers Forge resident-entry and process-supervision contracts, but its manifests supply fingerprint sources rather than callable invocation descriptors. Treating those files as executable commands advertised unavailable tools as available. Atlas context also has older fingerprint-only metadata.
desired_contract: Provider-declared fixed invocation argv/effects for read-only status and idempotent reconciliation, stable response schema, readiness fields, workspace identity, and bounded recovery. Atlas should publish its existing context invocation.
effect: Forge resident availability is not verified or automatically started by standard Environment entry; unsupported provider contracts remain discoverable with actionable diagnostics.
evidence: Forge .mncs/project.json revision 7 workspace-first-continuous-entry and continuous-process-supervision; Forge continuous.environment_enter already starts/reuses services and queries family_agent_context; dogfood selected entry reports Forge contracts as provider-invocation-undeclared. Atlas context-capsule uses registry/__main__.py through the explicit bootstrap adapter.
title: Provider evidence is not invocation or readiness addressing
why_not_local: Provider effects, startup semantics, process identity, JSON status meaning, and the correct CLI belong to the provider. Executing evidence modules would guess a protocol and can falsely report success.
workaround: Environment composes explicitly declared service probes/reconciliation under session authority; source fingerprints stay noncallable. The proven Atlas orientation adapter is retained in the small bootstrap table.

description: Entry observes a Language checkout revision and binds its exact release/debug executable, but file presence and executable permissions cannot establish which revision produced that binary or which runtime/features it actually supports. Selected native Test invocation passed, but that does not prove every bound toolchain operation.
desired_contract: Bounded provider-owned JSON toolchain inspection including binary build revision, compiler/runtime/schema versions, feature identities, and an actual readiness sentinel; status/reconciliation invocation declarations for Environment.
effect: Toolchain status is availability, not proof of source/binary compatibility. Native invocation proves the exercised capability only.
evidence: Dogfood session binds mncs-language/target/release/mncs, records observed checkout HEAD, and invokes mncs.test-result/1 successfully. CLI declarations separately select target/debug/mncs for several capabilities; no build-info/toolchain-info surface was found in crates/mncs-cli/src/main.rs.
title: Compiler executable cannot be tied to observed checkout readiness
why_not_local: Environment cannot infer compiler build provenance from Git HEAD or implement compiler/runtime feature semantics. Calling a binary present must remain a substrate observation.
workaround: Bind selected paths without ambient compiler fallback, probe permissions/toolchain presence, expose the verification basis, and exercise native provider contracts explicitly.

description: The existing background reconciler tests os.kill(pid, 0) against a PID file. A reused unrelated live PID can appear to be the reconciler; simultaneous daemon starts can race between checking and writing the PID file.
desired_contract: Exclusive daemon ownership lock plus process start identity and bounded heartbeat/readiness; consume the provider process-supervision contract for externally owned services.
effect: Background daemon PID status is not a verified service-readiness observation. Foreground health and declared provider probes are the canonical entry readiness checks.
evidence: mncs_env/reconciler.py Daemon.run and Daemon.status. This run added locking for foreground entry/reconciliation and workspace-scoped reconciler session selection, but did not launch or replace existing daemons.
owner: mncs-environment (follow-up); mncs-control / mncs-forge for reusable supervision contract
title: Environment reconciler process identity remains PID based
why_not_local: Environment owns hardening its own daemon, but should consume provider supervision for external services rather than create another general process supervisor.
workaround: Use foreground reconcile for deterministic entry recovery; do not kill or trust unrelated processes based on stale PID files.

description: Opening the canonical Store backend (EmbeddedStore construction plus verification) costs ~1.6s per process even before any read. Every mncs-env command pays it at least once, so entry/health/status latency is dominated by open cost rather than the work itself.
desired_contract: Sub-100ms Store open, or a documented persistent local handle / cheap generation probe that read-only commands can use without a full open.
effect: All store-backed commands take seconds; polling loops (status/health) are expensive.
evidence: mncs-environment session open measured at 1.6-1.9s with and without verify_on_open; entry paid it twice per invocation before the single-open change
title: Store open cost dominates every CLI command
why_not_local: Persistence lifecycle and verification live inside mncs-store; Environment cannot safely cache across processes without a store-owned handle or generation feed.
workaround: Single store open per entry; no-store file-side epoch fast path for status --terse; validated health epochs skip redundant revalidation and probes.

description: Providers publish diagnostics and invocation descriptors, but no family contract names a remediation capability (observe/repair/validate/envelope). Each orchestrator-to-provider remediation binding is currently a bilateral convention.
desired_contract: Family remediation capability shape: discovery suffix or manifest kind, argv/JSON envelope schema, effects/authority expectations, evidence routing (session artifact dir).
effect: Only mncs-doctor exposes remediation; other providers cannot be orchestrated until they adopt the bilateral convention.
evidence: mncs-environment/mncs_env/doctor.py defines the :repository-remediation suffix convention and consumes the mncs.doctor.remediation/1 envelope bilaterally with mncs-doctor
title: No family-standard remediation capability contract
why_not_local: A family capability contract must be standardized where providers coordinate; an Environment-only standard would fork the vocabulary.

description: Provider manifests expose verification/test argv with write effects. Session authority fail-closes on dirty/foreign/off-branch targets unless first claimed, so `mncs-env invoke ...` escalates before executing tests. This makes environment-native verification unavailable exactly while implementation branches are dirty.
desired_contract: Narrow verification/test effect class or scoped read-only test invocation contract; declared caches/output roots; explicit short-lived verification claims where writes are unavoidable.
effect: Native invoke cannot validate provider changes in active implementation branches; verification falls back to direct host unittest.
evidence: ses_4c9525caa5ca674e invoke mncs-automation:test/reconcile-tests returned pending-escalation: 'mncs-automation is not owned scope (dirty/foreign/off-branch); claim it first'; direct provider unittest fallback passed 14 tests.
title: Manifest verification commands cannot execute under session authority in dirty/foreign checkouts
why_not_local: Environment cannot silently downgrade declared effects or seize a dirty checkout for verification; providers own whether tests are hermetic/read-only and what authority they need.
workaround: Run the provider's declared argv directly in the checkout after confirming no other agent owns it; use environment invoke after the checkout is clean/claimed.

description: PATH `mncs` resolves to the offline validator/bootstrap CLI, while provider-local discovery expects the language compiler's `call` interface. Direct provider tests fail with validator usage unless MNCS_BIN selects the sibling release/debug compiler.
desired_contract: Distinct executable identities or provider-owned toolchain inspection/readiness; local discovery prefers the declared language checkout and validates `call` before use.
effect: Direct provider verification requires explicit toolchain env; the ambient path is safe only because provider invocation declares its toolchain.
evidence: mncs-doc/tools/project.py find_mncs order is explicit, MNCS_BIN, which mncs, then sibling debug/release; PATH /home/epi13/.local/bin/mncs lacks `call`; export MNCS_BIN=.../mncs-language/target/release/mncs makes 38 doc tests pass. Ambient environment is unaffected because capability toolchain_env supplies MNCS_BIN.
title: Offline MNCS executable shadows the language compiler on PATH
why_not_local: Environment cannot rename/replace user PATH tools or infer which `mncs` binary an executable is; providers/toolchain own binary identity and readiness.
workaround: Export MNCS_BIN to sibling mncs-language target/release/mncs for direct provider tests; prefer bound capability invocation in the environment.

description: Projection verification binds evidence to obligation + executor revision + subject (HEAD, worktree, input digest). The parallel ambient-verification track binds mncs.test.verification_coherence evidence to a richer family identity set (definition, subject, executor, toolchain, inventory, repository revision/fingerprint). Two evidence identity schemes now coexist.
desired_contract: One family evidence identity both tracks write and read; projection verdicts resolve from coherence records where available.
effect: Projection evidence and coherence evidence cannot yet be exchanged; toolchain/inventory drift does not invalidate projection evidence.
evidence: mncs_env/projection_verification.py evidence_id_for vs mncs-test native/mncs/test/verification_coherence.mncs CoherenceEvidence (campaign/ambient-verification-20261001, read-only survey)
title: Projection evidence vs coherence evidence identity convergence
why_not_local: Evidence identity is a family contract; unifying unilaterally would strand the coherence track's native policy.
workaround: Projection-local content-addressed evidence with executor-revision binding; immutable FAIL matches coherence semantics ('recorded FAIL is current knowledge').

description: Claim releases, verification resolutions, and Store generation changes emit no subscribable completion events, so continuous reconciliation runs on bounded-cadence epoch checks (projections --watch) instead of waking on the state transition itself.
desired_contract: Typed wake conditions (canonical > observed, block cleared, verdict resolved) evaluated natively with targeted reconcile invocation.
effect: Resident reconciliation notices change on the next tick (default 30s cadence) rather than immediately; quiet ticks still pay epoch observation.
evidence: mncs_env/cli.py cmd_projections_watch; mncs.automation.projection.v1 revisit_tick policy exists but no executor calls it
title: No event-driven projection wakeup
why_not_local: Wakeup ownership spans automation policy, Forge execution, and provider event feeds; an environment-local poller would harden into a competing scheduler.
workaround: Epoch-gated watch loop: quiet ticks reuse the epoch with no renders or native calls; lock held per tick only.

description: mncs-automation's reconcile suite (~19 tests, mostly native mncs call invocations) takes over 4 minutes wall-clock (~22s per test), so it cannot serve as an ambient verification executor: every new subject would stall the pass for minutes.
desired_contract: Native test execution fast enough for per-subject ambient verification, or a natively cached verdict the executor can quote.
effect: mncs-automation:rfc-index gates on mncs-doc's 2s self-check executor (cross-repo obligation) instead of its own suite.
evidence: python3 -m unittest tests.test_reconcile wall time >240s for 11 tests; mncs-doc tools/verify_projection.py ~2s PASS
title: Native test latency blocks full-suite verification executors
why_not_local: Per-call native latency is toolchain-owned; Environment cannot make the compiler faster from the outside.
workaround: Cross-repo obligation on the rendering provider's fast self-check; automation's own suite stays a merge gate, not an ambient executor.

description: Atlas owns canonical journal events, registry, and dashboard projections but declares no projections/verifications entries, so ambient coherence cannot yet observe or reconcile Atlas representations; branch is foreign-occupied.
desired_contract: Atlas declares projection consumers over shared store.projection.v1 rows and canonical journal events; dashboard/registry become reconciled projections.
effect: Atlas representations stay manually maintained; session evidence cannot yet flow into journal/media projections automatically.
evidence: Read-only survey 2026-10-01: mncs-atlas on campaign/family-context-convergence-20260918, .mncs/project.json has no projections section
title: Atlas has no projection-consumer surface yet
why_not_local: Atlas presentation semantics belong to Atlas; Environment only composes provider-declared projections.
workaround: Session evidence (mncs.session-evidence/1) records source identities, verdicts, and evidence references for future Atlas/journal/media consumption.

description: Ambient verification records evidence per session (verification_state + session evidence files). Two sessions observing exactly the same obligation definition, subject fingerprint, executor, toolchain, inventory, and repository generation still execute independently. Projection hardening now provides Store-backed immutable content-addressed evidence with CAS adoption, but verification evidence uses a different identity scheme and session-local storage (see prs_2b506a75686eb318).
desired_contract: Shared verification evidence rows keyed by the full coherence identity set, with originating-session provenance preserved; reuse only on exact equivalence.
effect: Duplicate test execution across concurrent sessions over identical subjects; no correctness issue, only redundant compute.
evidence: mncs_env/verification.py _measured_current identity set; mncs_env/projection_store.py write_evidence CAS; audit 2026-10-01 (spark-ambient-debug).
title: Cross-session verification evidence reuse needs unified identity + shared rows
why_not_local: Unifying on the session-local scheme would strand the convergence work; sharing must wait for one family evidence identity.
workaround: Per-session evidence; concurrent duplicate execution is correct but redundant.

description: Diagnostic witnesses are session-private. Two sessions over exactly the same failure (same obligation, test case, subject content, request, toolchain, depth) capture independently. Witnesses are content-addressed but the address covers session-local material (cwd, host facts), and no unified cross-session evidence identity exists (see prs_2b506a75686eb318, prs_verify_xsession_dedup).
desired_contract: Shared diagnostic evidence rows keyed by the failure binding plus depth, with originating-session provenance; reuse only on exact equivalence with single-flight capture.
effect: Duplicate witness capture across concurrent sessions over identical failures; no correctness issue, only redundant compute.
evidence: mncs_env/diagnostics.py session-private diagnostic_state; mncs_debug/runner.py witness_id material; audit 2026-10-01 (spark-ambient-debug).
title: Cross-session diagnostic evidence reuse needs unified identity + shared rows
why_not_local: Sharing on the current witness_id would confuse session-local material for equivalence; sharing must wait for one family evidence identity.
workaround: Per-session witnesses; concurrent duplicate capture is correct but redundant.

description: The background reconciler accepts commons/language sockets only through explicit CLI flags or environment variables. There is no provider-owned discovery of resident sockets for the janitor scope, so long-running semantic observation needs operator wiring per workspace.
desired_contract: Provider-published resident registry (workspace -> socket/lease/identity) readable by the janitor without lifecycle authority, or a declared per-workspace socket binding in the environment definition.
effect: Long-running agents notice semantic changes only when the operator wires each workspace socket explicitly.
evidence: mncs_env/cli.py --commons-socket/--language-socket threading into reconciler.build_sources; mncs-language-service provider owns socket paths but publishes no janitor-scoped discovery
title: Janitor sessions lack provider-owned resident discovery
why_not_local: Socket paths, lease ownership, and workspace binding belong to the providers; an environment-local convention table would drift from provider reality.
workaround: Pass --language-socket per workspace (or MNLS_SERVICE_SOCKET for one); entry-time semantics pass covers declared workspaces without the daemon.

description: store_backend resolves the mncs-store Python package through a fixed parents[2] sibling fallback from its own file location. Provider worktrees nested deeper (repo/.worktrees/<slug>) miss the fallback, so every store-backed test needs MNCS_STORE_PYTHON set explicitly.
desired_contract: Git-aware family-root discovery with an explicit override, identical from any checkout depth.
effect: Worktree-isolated development pays a manual environment tax; fresh agents meet 30+ spurious failures.
evidence: mncs_env/store_backend.py _load_store_api parents[2] fallback; worktree suite runs fail with StoreUnavailable unless MNCS_STORE_PYTHON is exported
title: Fixed-depth sibling fallback breaks worktree checkouts
why_not_local: It is local: resolution should walk to the enclosing family root (git-aware) or require explicit binding instead of a fixed depth.
workaround: Export MNCS_STORE_PYTHON (and MNCS_TEST_FAMILY) when running the suite from a worktree.

description: The valid-campaign-entry compactness test asserts inspect output exceeds entry context, and is red on main: successive ambient blocks (doctor, projection, verification) grew entry context past inspect output with no budget or per-block accounting.
desired_contract: Explicit byte budgets per entry block plus a compactness assertion that names the over-budget block.
effect: Compactness regressions are invisible until a coarse assertion trips; campaigns cannot tell whether their block is the cause.
evidence: tests/test_environment.py::EntryFrictionTests::test_valid_campaign_entry_is_compact_and_uses_isolated_state red on main (3889 vs 4089); undeclared sessions now carry no semantic block
title: Entry context has no per-block byte budget
why_not_local: It is local: the budget (or the assertion shape) belongs to the entry contract.
workaround: Keep new entry blocks terse, symmetric, and omitted when unconfigured; record measured footprints per block in campaign reports.
